text:
elaine: Quick summary from today's bring-up: ran phi-7b-int4 and phi-7b-int8 across our standard chat+summarize evals. initial numbers look like int4 cuts cost ~2.8x versus fp16, int8 ~1.9x. quality delta: int4 BLEU-ish/QA drops ~1.6% relative to int8 on our prompts.

sam: can you paste the unit econ snippet? want to validate against the GTN assumptions (latency target 120ms p50).

elaine: sure — rough math from the bench (prod-like batch mix):
```
throughput (tokens/sec/GPU): fp16=5400, int8=9200, int4=15000
cost/GPU/hour (on dedicated pool): $3.6 (amortized infra)
tokens_per_hour: throughput * 3600
cost_per_1M_tokens: (cost/GPU/hour) / (tokens_per_hour) * 1e6
=> fp16 ~ $0.67 / 1M, int8 ~ $0.39 / 1M, int4 ~ $0.24 / 1M
```

carla: nice. What's the quality tradeoff on our user-facing summarization task? product-ryan needs that for pricing guidance.

elaine: eval score (RWD-Summ metric) averaged over seed set (n=1k): fp16=0.78, int8=0.775, int4=0.762. So int8 is within noise, int4 shows a small but consistent regression on coherence/long-range facts.

perf-bot: CI-run: 1719876400 -> latency p50/p95 (int8): 98ms / 210ms; (int4): 110ms / 320ms under mixed load.

shreyas: hm p95 for int4 looks bad under mixed load — might violate UI SLOs if we route 100% traffic. Could consider hybrid routing: majority to int8, spill to int4 for low-cost requests or non-fidelity features.

sam: agree. propose risk tiers:
- tier A (high-fidelity): fp16 or int8 fallback (cost higher)
- tier B (standard UX): int8 primary, fp16 fallback on hallucination triggers
- tier C (low-cost bulk ops): int4 for batch summarization where latency constraints looser

product-ryan: need a concise recommendation for GTN: what % cost saving if we shift 60% traffic to int4 under hybrid and keep 40% int8?

elaine: back-of-envelope: current mix = 100% int8 baseline. cost_per_1M int8=$0.39. if 60% -> int4 ($0.24) and 40% int8 => blended = 0.6*0.24 + 0.4*0.39 = $0.298 / 1M => ~23.5% savings vs all-int8.
quality_blend: 0.6*0.762 + 0.4*0.775 = 0.7686 (~0.6% drop vs all-int8)

carla: that seems like a good sweet spot. But we should quantify regression impact on top-10 product prompts. can we run a targeted eval set (GTN sample) overnight?

elaine: yes queued a run with 5k GTN prompts, will have diffs tomorrow. added a canary plan: start 5% int4 traffic on dedicated pool, compare error/rollback metrics.

shreyas: also we need a guardrail for p95 latency spikes — route to int8 automatically if queue depth > X or p95 > 250ms. ops-playbook entry?

sam: I'll draft the ops-playbook snippet. also can we add a lightweight quality monitor that alerts if coherence metric drops >0.8% over 1h window?

elaine: done — alert rule created in console (eval-rule:phi-7b-hybrid-qual).

product-ryan: for GTN messaging: recommended copy — "Up to ~24% inference cost savings with hybrid quantized routing while retaining >99% of task quality for standard summarization workloads; enterprise SLAs available for high-fidelity variants." ok?

carla: tweak to include latency note: "Savings at comparable p50 latency; p95 dependent on workload — canary recommended."

product-ryan: updated. thanks.

elaine: follow-ups: overnight GTN run id=20240117-phi7b-hybrid-1, canary scheduled 0300 UTC. will post results in this thread tomorrow. :thumbsup:
